HONESTY-1_matmul_tflops_misrepresentatio.original_issue: matmul_f32_tiled.axc @strategy{tile_m,tile_n} holes are inert (never referenced in kernel body); bench was labeled 'matmul TFLOPS' / 'AXIOM-Compute matmul performance'
HONESTY-1_matmul_tflops_misrepresentatio.resolution_in_spec: RESOLVED. r1 reframes the milestone deliverable to the RESIDENT-TIMING METHODOLOGY (not a competitive matmul number). The headline bench is now `resident_timing_kernels` reporting kernel-only ns over EXISTING real kernels (saxpy, q4km matvec/matmul, coopmat matmul_tile). The naive GEMM bench is RENAMED `naive_gemm_harness_validation` and its printed line explicitly states 'NAIVE un-tiled scalar f32 GEMM (harness validation only — NOT an optimized matmul; expect low single-digit % of cuBLAS; real tiling is M3.2)'. AT-1581 guards that the printed string contains 'NAIVE' and 'harness validation' so the label cannot silently regress. The example file fix (remove @strategy line, reword header/intent) is mandated as HANDOFF-0 and appears in files_to_modify for matmul_f32_tiled.axc. Competitive matmul TFLOPS is explicitly deferred to M3.2.
HONESTY-1_matmul_tflops_misrepresentatio.verified_in_example_file: The example file (matmul_f32_tiled.axc) still contains the old @strategy line and comments AT DESIGN TIME — but this is expected: the file is in files_to_modify and HANDOFF-0 is the Coder's FIRST task. AT-1576 regression-gates that the file compiles without a @strategy block after the edit. The spec is correct; execution is the Coder's phase.

TIMING-1_honest_labeling.original_issue: TOP_OF_PIPE->BOTTOM_OF_PIPE span incorrectly called 'kernel-only ALU time'; CpuFenceWall quoted as kernel time; warmup only recommended not mandatory
TIMING-1_honest_labeling.resolution_in_spec: RESOLVED. r1 renames the measured quantity to 'GPU dispatch duration — TOP_OF_PIPE→BOTTOM_OF_PIPE timestamp span covering the single dispatch; EXCLUDES host upload/readback; INCLUDES dispatch launch + pipeline latency'. Module header reword is explicitly mandated (HANDOFF-16). Warmup-discard elevated to MANDATORY: 2 untimed warm-up dispatches, report MIN-of-N (N=10 bench, N>=3 AT-1530). CpuFenceWall is explicitly labeled '— scheduling-inclusive, NOT a GPU kernel time' everywhere it appears (AT-1582 guards). Query pool is NOT created when timestampValidBits==0 OR timestampPeriod==0 (per HANDOFF-3 / select_timing_source helper), so no vkCmdWriteTimestamp is ever recorded on a 0-valid-bits queue.

CORRECTNESS-1_workgroup_guard.original_issue: dispatch_resident lacked a workgroup-count check; guard was only in the bench, not in the library method; any non-bench caller of dispatch_resident could trigger an out-of-range validation error or hang
CORRECTNESS-1_workgroup_guard.resolution_in_spec: RESOLVED. dispatch_resident now calls the existing validate_request workgroup guard (max_compute_work_group_count check) on cfg.workgroups at the TOP of the method, BEFORE any GPU work, returning DispatchError::WorkgroupCountExceedsDeviceLimit. Guard lives in the LIBRARY METHOD, not in callers. AT-1579 added (pure/Lavapipe-testable: out-of-range workgroups rejected). The bench pre-shrink is retained as a friendly UX check but is now subsumed by the library guard.

CORRECTNESS-2_upload_partial_failure_cle.original_issue: No RAII guard for partially-created Vulkan objects inside upload_resident; a failure mid-allocation would leak device-local buffers, descriptor pool, staging buffers, etc.
CORRECTNESS-2_upload_partial_failure_cle.resolution_in_spec: RESOLVED. upload_resident builds persistent objects into local Options; an explicit cleanup_partial_resident helper (CORRECTNESS-2, HANDOFF-8) destroys already-created objects in REVERSE creation order (query_pool, fence, command_pool, descriptor_pool, staging_bufs, device_local_bufs) at every early-return Err after the first allocation. Transient upload staging buffer and transient CB/pool are freed on their own error paths. ResidentBuffers is constructed ONLY when ALL objects exist, so Drop never double-frees. AT-1580 documents the cleanup-ordering contract for QA to verify against the diff.

PREFLIGHT_additive_decision.original_issue: prepare_kernel_checked additive vs folding in — spec must switch bench/tests to checked variant and stop claiming the gap is 'closed' for raw prepare_kernel callers
PREFLIGHT_additive_decision.resolution_in_spec: RESOLVED. Decision is documented and justified: folding in would break prepare_kernel's signature (it lacks coopmat/kernel_name params). prepare_kernel_checked is ADDITIVE. Driver/bench/test paths SWITCHED to checked variant (HANDOFF-10/11). Milestone summary explicitly states the gap is 'closeable opt-in', not 'closed'. Future milestone may fold in once KernelHandleInner carries the coopmat shape.

WARNING_warmup_mandatory.original_issue: Warmup was 'RECOMMENDED'; should be MANDATORY to prevent first-iter outlier skewing AT-1530
WARNING_warmup_mandatory.resolution_in_spec: ELEVATED TO MANDATORY. 2 untimed warm-up dispatch_resident calls discarded, MIN-of-N reported. HANDOFF-12 explicit. AT-1530 updated to discard warm-up before the measured samples. Open_question shows RESOLVED.

WARNING_cpufencewall_labeling.original_issue: CpuFenceWall number returned under same kernel_ns field; bench/AT-1530 could quote it as a kernel time
WARNING_cpufencewall_labeling.resolution_in_spec: RESOLVED via AT-1582 and HANDOFF-13. If timing_source==CpuFenceWall, bench appends '— scheduling-inclusive, NOT a GPU kernel time'. AT-1530 skips the smaller-than assertion on Lavapipe. The GpuTimestamp enum comment in resident.rs still says 'Accurate kernel-only time' — acceptable given the surrounding caveats, but the Coder should harmonize with the module-header reword per HANDOFF-16.
WARNING_cpufencewall_labeling.minor_note: ResidentTimingSource::GpuTimestamp doc comment ('Accurate kernel-only time') is slightly optimistic vs the module-header reword ('GPU dispatch duration, includes pipeline latency') — but this is a minor documentation drift that does not affect correctness; HANDOFF-16 covers module-header prose and the Coder can align the enum comment at the same time.

WARNING_query_pool_on_zero_validbits.original_issue: Query pool was created unconditionally; on devices with timestampValidBits==0 recording vkCmdWriteTimestamp is a validation error
WARNING_query_pool_on_zero_validbits.resolution_in_spec: RESOLVED. Per HANDOFF-3: when select_timing_source(valid_bits, period)==CpuFenceWall, the query pool is NOT created in upload_resident (query_pool = vk::QueryPool::null()) and NO vkCmdWriteTimestamp is recorded in dispatch_resident. The timing source is decided ONCE from snapshotted valid_bits/period at upload time.

FIELD_DOC_FIX.original_issue: resident.rs uses_coopmat field comment incorrectly says 'shaderInt16 (for diagnostics)'
FIELD_DOC_FIX.resolution_in_spec: Explicitly mandated in HANDOFF-16 and FIELD-DOC-FIX changelog entry. Coder fixes to 'Diagnostic-only: whether these buffers back a coopmat kernel. Set false in M3.1.5 (handle carries no coopmat flag).' Confirmed needed — current resident.rs line 104 reads: 'Whether these buffers need shaderInt16 (for diagnostics).'

strengths: HONESTY-1 resolution is thorough and structurally sound: the milestone deliverable is correctly reframed as the resident-timing methodology, NOT a competitive matmul number. The two-bench split (resident_timing_kernels for honest ns, naive_gemm_harness_validation with mandatory labeling) is the minimal clean fix that preserves all existing machinery while making the thesis-honesty violation impossible to reintroduce silently (AT-1581 is a label guard, not just a documentation note).

TIMING-1 resolution is precise: the terminology shift from 'kernel-only ALU time' to 'GPU dispatch duration (TOP→BOTTOM, includes pipeline latency, excludes upload/readback)' is accurate and matches Vulkan spec §18.2 semantics. The 'measured quantity vs dispatch_handle' framing gives a clear, honest interpretation of what the timing proves. External validation: Khronos Vulkan-Samples timestamp_queries sample uses the identical TOP_OF_PIPE→BOTTOM_OF_PIPE pattern with the same prose (https://github.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Samples/blob/main/samples/performance/timestamp_queries/timestamp_queries.cpp).

CORRECTNESS-1 guard placement in the library (dispatch_resident) rather than only in callers is the correct API-safety decision. validate_request's workgroup branch is already proven in AT-1519+; moving it into dispatch_resident means every future caller is protected without needing to remember a pre-check. AT-1579 is Lavapipe-testable and does not require an oversized GPU.

CORRECTNESS-2 explicit cleanup_partial_resident helper is the correct pattern over incremental RAII: it makes the cleanup order AUDITABLE (QA can grep for each early return) without requiring Option-wrapped fields in a struct whose Drop already handles the fully-constructed case. Reverse-creation-order teardown is the standard Vulkan object lifecycle requirement (Vulkan spec §3.3.3 Object Lifetime). AT-1580 as a QA diff-read item is an honest acknowledgment that full fault-injection testing is impractical on real GPU hardware.

The select_timing_source(valid_bits, period) pure helper gives a deterministic, unit-testable boundary for the GpuTimestamp/CpuFenceWall decision (AT-1573). Snapshotting the values at upload time means a single ResidentBuffers never flips paths mid-life — no stale-result hazard across the N-iteration dispatch loop.

prepare_kernel_checked additive design with a factored preflight_kernel_support private helper (HANDOFF-10) cleanly separates the safety check from the Vulkan object creation. The HONEST gap statement ('closeable opt-in, not universally closed') is accurate and prevents the milestone summary from overclaiming. AT-1574/1578 test the preflight in isolation without GPU.

AT-1577 regression gate (cargo test + clippy -D warnings + bench builds + bench IDs match honest set + spirv-val unchanged) is a comprehensive, automatable exit criterion that catches any drift back toward the misleading matmul_tflops_4096 bench ID.

OPT-NOTE-2 (transient upload staging vs retained readback staging, no aliasing) and OPT-NOTE-3 (readback call-order contract: upload→dispatch(s)→readback) are correctly documented as spec-level contracts with // comment requirements, reducing the chance of Coder confusion on the staging buffer lifecycle.
The 50 GB cap assertion is correctly placed in the bench (not the library), consistent with CLAUDE.md hard rule #1 and HANDOFF-12/OPT-NOTE-4. 4096² f32 ×3 ≈ 192 MB is trivially under the cap.
concerns: Minor: resident.rs module header still reads 'kernel-only timing' on line 17 ('giving kernel-only timing') and ResidentTimingSource::GpuTimestamp doc still reads 'Accurate kernel-only time' on line 56. HANDOFF-16 mandates rewording lines 21-34; the Coder should extend that reword to line 17 and the enum doc to align with the honest 'GPU dispatch duration' framing. This is a prose drift risk, not a correctness risk — the runtime behavior is governed by select_timing_source, not the comment.

Minor: AT-1530 description says 'timing_source==GpuTimestamp AND min kernel_ns < measured dispatch_handle wall ns (margin)' — the 'margin' is unspecified. To prevent flakiness, the Coder should use a concrete relative margin (e.g., kernel_ns < 0.5 * dispatch_handle_ns) that is wide enough to be robust across GPU frequency states but narrow enough to catch a regression where upload/readback time is inadvertently included. The spec doesn't pin the margin; QA should flag if the test is written with a tight absolute margin.

Minor: The open_question 'RESOLVED (warmup)' entry says 'report MIN-of-N (N=10 bench, N>=3 AT-1530)' but N=3 is a very small sample for a GPU timing assertion on a real device under clock-management variability. This is acceptable for a design review pass but QA and the pessimistic code reviewer should verify the Coder uses N>=5 post-warmup samples for AT-1530 to avoid a single-outlier flake on NVIDIA Blackwell under boost-clock ramp.
validation_against_existing: Vulkan spec §18.2 (Query Operations): vkCmdResetQueryPool must appear in the same CB before vkCmdWriteTimestamp — HANDOFF-2 explicitly mandates cmd_reset_query_pool as the FIRST recorded command. The spec has removed the query-pool-created-unconditionally defect by tying creation to select_timing_source==GpuTimestamp (HANDOFF-3). https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/latest/html/vkspec.html#queries-operation-time

Vulkan spec §3.3.3 (Object Lifetime): objects must be destroyed before their parent; cleanup_partial_resident reverse-creation-order teardown honors this. The fully-constructed Drop (resident.rs:127-162) already does this correctly and is unchanged. https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/latest/html/vkspec.html#fundamentals-objectmodel-lifetime

KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Samples timestamp_queries: uses TOP_OF_PIPE→BOTTOM_OF_PIPE span for 'GPU execution time of a single draw/dispatch', same convention as r1 spec. The sample's prose calls it 'execution time' (not ALU time) — matching the r1 'GPU dispatch duration' label. https://github.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Samples/blob/main/samples/performance/timestamp_queries/timestamp_queries.cpp

NVIDIA Nsight documentation on timestampPeriod==0 behavior (e.g., Lavapipe / Mesa software): the driver returns 0 for timestampPeriod when GPU timestamps are not meaningful; vkCmdWriteTimestamp on a queue with timestampValidBits==0 is explicitly undefined behavior per the spec. r1's gate (select_timing_source returns CpuFenceWall when period==0 OR valid_bits==0, no query pool created) is the correct portable workaround. https://docs.nvidia.com/nsight-systems/

llama.cpp Vulkan backend (ggml-org/llama.cpp#16230, #17273): the resident-timing methodology (upload weights once, dispatch N times, time only the dispatch span) directly mirrors how production Vulkan inference benchmarks measure kernel throughput vs host-overhead-inclusive wall time. This framing is validated by the llama.cpp beachhead rationale in CLAUDE.md.

Sakana AI CUDA Engineer / STARK prior art: the project thesis (annotation-first verified intent) is reinforced by r1's HONESTY-1 fix — presenting a naive un-tiled scalar GEMM as 'matmul TFLOPS' would be exactly the label-gaming those systems are vulnerable to. r1 eliminates this by mandatory labeling and deferring competitive numbers to a properly-tiled M3.2 kernel.
test_suggestions: AT-1530 N>=3 post-warmup samples: consider raising to N>=5 in the test (N=10 is already specified for the bench). Three samples on a real GPU under boost-clock management is borderline; five gives more confidence in the MIN-of-N assertion.

AT-1530 margin: the spec says 'kernel_ns < measured dispatch_handle wall ns (margin)' without pinning the margin. Recommend Coder uses kernel_ns < dispatch_handle_ns / 2 (50% headroom) — wide enough to survive clock ramp, narrow enough to catch a regression where upload time leaks into the resident measurement.

HANDOFF-16 reword scope: Coder should extend the module-header reword to resident.rs line 17 ('giving kernel-only timing') and ResidentTimingSource::GpuTimestamp doc comment ('Accurate kernel-only time') to match the honest 'GPU dispatch duration' language, not just lines 21-34.
summary: All five issues raised by the Pessimistic reviewer are fully and correctly addressed in r1: HONESTY-1 (inert @strategy holes, misleading TFLOPS label) is resolved by reframing the milestone to the resident-timing methodology and mandating explicit 'NAIVE / harness validation only' labeling with AT-1581 as a regression guard; TIMING-1 (honest timing semantics, mandatory warmup, CpuFenceWall falleling) is resolved by precise prose, mandatory warmup-discard, AT-1582 label guard, and query-pool creation gated on select_timing_source; CORRECTNESS-1 (workgroup guard) moves the check into the library method with AT-1579; CORRECTNESS-2 (partial-failure cleanup) adds cleanup_partial_resident with reverse-order teardown and AT-1580 QA audit; and the PREFLIGHT decision is honestly documented as 'closeable opt-in, not universally closed'. Remaining concerns are minor prose drifts and a recommendation to raise AT-1530's sample count — neither blocks implementation. The r1 spec is ready to proceed to Coder.
